newsitem.title: UK: BONDS SUPPORT FIRM START FOR EUROMARKETS.
newsitem.headline: BONDS SUPPORT FIRM START FOR EUROMARKETS.

text.p: European financial markets opened firmer on Friday, finding support from solid performances by bonds and currencies but potentially likely to suffer a lack of direction from the absence of important data.
New York's Dow Jones Industrial average closed 8.5 points down on Thursday on weak U.S. durable goods orders, failing to give much leadership to Europe.
But London's FTSE 100 advanced in early trading on Friday, fuelled by sharp gains in the British pharmaceutical sector and a strong gilt and a steady to firm bond market, traders said.
By the middle of the morning the index was up 18 points at the day's high, with advancers leading decliners by a margin of more than five to three.
"As long as we get continual gearing from the bond and gilt markets, I think the FTSE can go forward," said one trader, who is targeting the 4,100 level by the end of the year.

Markets were taking some cognisance of some low-key U.S. data later on Friday, with the second quarter real domestic product figure due at 1230 GMT and Michigan September consumer confidence data due to 1400.

In Paris, French shares started higher, supported by a firm bond market, with stock market analysts saying the trend was bullish. "The market is still far from being technically overbought," said one.
The blue-chip CAC 40 index was up around five points by the middle of the morning.
Economist interpreted data showing French unemployment jumped to a record high in August of 12.6 percent as underlining the need for lower interest rates in France.
Trade remained robust with data showing France had a seasonally adjusted trade surplus in July of 11.10 billion francs ($2.16 billion) compared with a revised surplus in June of 9.78 billion.
Germany bucked the trend somewhat, with shares trading lower in early bourse dealings, hit by profit-taking ahead of the weekend after the DAX Index reached a new record high on Thursday.
